text:
alicia: quick follow-up from the stream-lease RFC — I want to nail down the exact handshake semantics we expect at the gateway + edge proxy boundary when we allow resumable streaming. There were a few open Qs:

alicia: 1) When a client retries a streaming call after a midstream disconnect, do we require an explicit resume token header from the client to attempt resume, or can any idempotent request attempt auto-resume if the proxy has cached state?

ben: my preference: require explicit resume token. implicit resume at the proxy is risky across multi-hop and tenant boundaries. token makes intent explicit and avoids accidental duplication. :+1:

marta: agree with @ben. also the token should be short-lived and opaque. we should define TTL and a revocation path (in case of replays or leaked tokens).

sam: small counterpoint — for first-party SDKs we could offer "best-effort resume" where SDK includes a signed resume token automatically, falling back to non-resumable. but core gateway contract should be explicit resume header.

alicia: ok explicit it is. proposed header names: `X-Resume-Token` (opaque base64), `X-Resume-Offset` (optional int, token can encode offset too). thoughts?

ben: +1. also add `X-Resume-Model-Variant` so resume fails fast if model variant changed. resume should be conservative: if variant mismatch -> reject resume and suggest full replay.

marta: agree on variant header. we should also document failure modes and recommended client behavior: if resume rejected, client must retry with full request and dedup logic on the app side if they have side-effects.

alicia: regarding memory/accounting — proxies will need to persist minimal KV for active leases. we cannot hold full KV cache indefinitely. proposal: maintain resume metadata (token -> pointer to persisted snapshot) for TTL (default 30s) and evict sooner under memory pressure. If pointer expired, resume fails.

sam: can we use a disk-backed LRU for pointers? keep pointer + small metadata in memory, snapshot on local SSD. saves RAM.

ben: fine, but then we need to surface SLOs: resume success probability vs eviction window. ops needs visibility.

infra-bot: Deploy note: resumption-store v2 rolled to canary env. config `resume_ttl_seconds` = 30 by default.

marta: tracing/observability concern: tag traces with `resume.attempt=true|false` and `resume.result=success|expired|variant_mismatch|invalid_token`. that will make postmortems easier.

alicia: agree. also we need to ensure billing semantics: if resume succeeds we should continue charging from original call's token bucket or attach a resume-id to attribute usage. if resume fails and client retries new request, that counts as a new call (maybe billed separately). ops: do we have a way to attribute resumed tokens to the original billing record?

ben: add `Resume-Origin-ID` (opaque) embedded in token that maps to billing record. token lifetime must match billing record retention. if origin record missing treat as new call.

sam: security: tokens must be HMAC-signed by control plane, include nonce and expiry. don't accept unsigned tokens from clients.

marta: also, make it explicit: proxies should never accept resume tokens minted by other tenants. token should encode tenant id and proxy must validate.

alicia: ok security + tenant checks are a must. next: API shape for non-resumable fallback. clients should be able to request `Prefer: resumable=true` and gateway returns `Accept-Resume: yes|no` in the immediate response headers so SDKs can opt-in.

ben: I like that. makes feature discovery easy. default behavior: gateway replies `Accept-Resume: yes` only if the upstream path and model support it and there is sufficient memory budget. otherwise `no`.

sam: implementationally the gateway needs to check model variant compatibility and capacity before advertising resume acceptance. that'll add some cold-path checks but ok.

marta: small nit: we should ensure `Accept-Resume` is returned atomically with a 200/202 start-of-stream response so clients can decide whether to start streaming tokens locally or rely on server-side resume.

alicia: for hedging and fallback: if the gateway attempts resume and upstream rejects (variant mismatch), we should automatically attempt a non-resume fallback path for the client only if client included `Prefer: auto-fallback=true`. otherwise return `409 ResumeRejected` with a short message.

ben: yes, and make `409` machine-readable JSON with error_code `resume_rejected` + hint header `Accept-Resume: no` to simplify SDK logic.

marta: logging: log truncated token hash not full token for privacy. store only a 128-bit keyed hash for debug mapping.

alicia: action items: 
- define token payload fields + signing (sam)
- update gateway advertizing protocol + Accept-Resume header (ben)
- implement TTL + eviction metrics + resume trace tags (marta)
- SDK guidance doc for best-effort resume and auto-fallback (alicia)

sam: I'll draft token spec and paste minimal proto snippet here.

sam: ```
message ResumeTokenPayload {
  string tenant_id = 1;
  string origin_call_id = 2;
  uint64 offset = 3;
  uint32 expiry_unix = 4;
  string model_variant = 5;
  bytes nonce = 6;
}
// token = base64(HMAC_SIGN(signing_key, payload_bytes) || payload_bytes)
```

marta: looks good. add `billing_record_id` optional field.

sam: added, will post PR to the RFC repo with examples.

alicia: thanks. one more UX ask: can we provide a `resume-preview` endpoint for SDKs to validate resume token without starting a full stream? e.g., `POST /v1/resume/preview` returns `200` with small `stream_head` if resume possible, else error.

ben: that helps debugging but doubles an extra call from SDKs. prefer we rely on `Accept-Resume` and quick resume attempt. still, preview could be behind feature flag for internal SDKs.

marta: fine w/ feature flag. operational cost should be measured.

alicia: great. I'll summarize and open a follow-up RFC PR with the headers, token spec, TTL defaults, and the error codes. assigning the checklist above. thanks everyone. :rocket:
